data.exact_reserve_text: During 2014 the net loss ratio (net of acquisitions costs) on certain lines of business for the 2012 and prior years of account was increased. These increases are set out in the table below together with their effect on ultimate claims reserves.

prior_year_events.impact_description: The 2012 and prior underwriting years produced a loss of GBP 17,854k. The result was affected by worse than expected claims experienced primarily in the US liability account and further movement in the discontinued element of the Treaty account.
Deterioration arises on the 2013 and prior years of account and emanates primarily from the Liability account which is no longer written in that form.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a strengthening of prior year reserves by GBP 23.342 million in 2014, primarily driven by an increase in ultimate claims reserves for the Treaty and Liability lines of business from the 2012 and prior years of account. This adverse development was linked to increased net loss ratios in these segments. Additionally, the 2012 and prior underwriting years produced a loss of GBP 17.854 million due to worse than expected claims, particularly in the US liability account and the discontinued element of the Treaty account.

worse than expected claims experienced primarily in the US liability account

data.data_quality_notes: The 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' note on page 14 states 'net loss ratio (net of acquisitions costs) ... was increased' but then quantifies 'Increase in claims reserves (GBP 000)'. The quantified amount is assumed to be gross, but the preceding text refers to 'net loss ratio'.
